To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we propose a novel approach to unsupervised domain adaption for classification problems in the presence of non-stochastic missing components in the target domain, which is shown to outperform state of the art methods on two different datasets.

(i) we introduce a novel unsupervised domain adaptive imputation model that performs well under various divergence families, and (ii) we demonstrate its performance on a digit benchmark and on real world digital advertising data, and we analyze it in detail.

(1) we propose a model that can perform joint domain adaptation, missing data imputation and classification, (2) we show that the proposed model outperforms baselines on a digit recognition task, (3) we show that this model outperforms the baselines on real world digital advertising data.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following problem: given an unsupervised dataset from a target domain, where some components are systematically missing, how to perform domain adaptation with this dataset, in order to classify the missing data.
unsupervised domain-adaptation for classification in the presence of non-stochastic missing components in the target domain.

the following problem: Given a source domain $\mathcal{S}$ and a target domain $\mathcal{T}$, where $\mathcal{X} \subseteq \mathcal{S} \cap \mathcal{T}$ and $\mathcal{Y} \subseteq \{1, \dots, k\}$, we consider an unsupervised domain adaptive classification task with missing data.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our proposed approach is a very good solution for the problem of unsupervised domain adaption with missing data.
our method performs well on real world digital advertising problems and is a step towards solving real-world problems with domain adaptation and missing data.
our model is able to adapt to a new domain with non-stochastic missing features and achieve a better performance compared to a standard domain adaptation approach.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose a way to jointly learn domain adaptation and imputation for classification, with an algorithm that can be applied under various divergence assumptions.
our model can be seen as a domain adaptation model that is robust to missing data, and as an imputation model that can leverage domain adaptation to perform better.
we propose a new model that performs domain adaptation and imputation jointly, that is shown to perform better than state-of-the-art baselines in both domains.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in the case where the missing data are non-stochastic, imputation and domain adaptation can be jointly performed in a single model.
, in the presence missing data, it is beneficial to explicitly impute them during domain adaptation.
imputing missing data in an unsupvervised setting is beneficial for classification performance, even if the missingness pattern is not known.
